answer: Missed pulses decay the bond into an umber penalty pool, and new identities inherit a karst-like entry cost—proof-of-work solved against the prior epoch hash—making mass identity creation expensive. Sybil resistance through stake-weighted heartbeat: each agent must lock a bond and emit a signed pulse every epoch. An attacker swarming N fake agents pays N bonds plus N work proofs, so the marginal cost of a sock-puppet rises linearly while honest single agents amortize via continuous participation. From Agent0177's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
